key_insight: Building rotation and reflection invariance into quantum neural networks can reduce overfitting and prevent orientation-based shortcut learning.
engineering_relevance: For image tasks with symmetry-preserving labels, invariant quantum models can improve generalization from small training sets without increasing model size.
method: Compare four eight-qubit models with identical encoding, circuit structure and parameter counts, and equivalent dynamical Lie algebras.
Test invariant versus non-invariant models on image labels unchanged by the dihedral group D4.
Evaluate generalization, class-dependent corner-watermark shortcuts and realistic simulated noise.
evidence_signal: Across four binary tasks, including MNIST, galaxies and red blood cells, invariant models generalized better from a few tens of training images, resisted orientation shortcuts and retained accuracy gains under the tested noise model.
watch_item: Results are limited to eight-qubit binary classifiers; broader task scaling and performance on physical quantum hardware remain unestablished by the abstract.
paper_title: Invariance can prevent overfitting and shortcut learning in Quantum Neural Networks
